title: Medication Safety Fundamentals
description: Foundational quiz on safe administration, verification, and patient monitoring.

questions.prompt: Which action should the nurse take first before administering digoxin to an adult client?

choices.text: Check the apical pulse for one full minute.
Offer the medication with a potassium supplement.
Encourage the client to ambulate after the dose.
Administer the medication with an antacid.

questions.explanation: Digoxin slows the heart rate via vagal stimulation and direct SA/AV node effects. The nurse must assess the apical pulse for a full 60 seconds before administration and withhold the drug if the adult rate falls below 60 bpm, notifying the provider.
questions.rationale: Digoxin has a narrow therapeutic index; bradycardia is both a side effect and a sign of toxicity. Pulse assessment before each dose is a fundamental nursing responsibility and directly supports safe medication administration practice.

distractorRationale.B: Potassium supplements may be appropriate in hypokalemic clients taking digoxin (hypokalemia increases toxicity risk), but they are not the pre-administration safety check — pulse assessment must occur first.
distractorRationale.C: Ambulation is not related to pre-administration safety assessment for a cardiac glycoside.
distractorRationale.D: Antacids are not routinely paired with digoxin; this reflects a common misconception about cardiac medications and is not a standard nursing action before administration.

questions.prompt: Which statements reflect the rights of medication administration? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: The traditional rights of medication administration include: right patient, right medication, right dose, right route, right time, and right documentation. 'Right roommate' is not a recognized right and is a deliberate distractor.
questions.rationale: The six rights of medication administration form a systematic safety checklist to prevent medication errors, which are among the most common preventable adverse events in acute care settings and a priority NCLEX content area.

distractorRationale.D: 'Right roommate' is a nonsensical distractor designed to test whether learners can distinguish genuine patient-safety rights from fabricated options.
